user_questions.question: Who should receive the low-stock alert? Options: (a) the storefront record owner, an internal User (all 21 storefronts are owned by 'OrgFarm EPIC'), via in-app notification or email; (b) the storefront's Primary_Contact__c, a Contact (all 21 populated, all with email), via email; (c) both. Recommendation: (b), since it is the storefront-specific person.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Alert the storefront's Primary Contact when below threshold.

user_questions.question: How should 'runs low' be defined and what should be tracked? Options: (a) a new Inventory Item record per storefront with quantity on hand, unit of measure, and a per-item reorder threshold; (b) a single org-wide threshold value. Recommendation: (a).
user_questions.simulated_answer: New Inventory Item object per storefront with quantity, unit, reorder threshold; alert when below threshold.

skill_friction: D2 skip rule: SKILL.md allows skipping D2 only if D1 and step-3 queries answered its questions; for a greenfield object the queries covered all D2 topics, but the skill does not say explicitly whether 'no objects in scope exist yet' justifies skipping D2. Skipped and covered with trigger/flow/dependency queries.

Wrong-claim counting: Rule 3 counts distinct wrong claims including platform claims that cannot be tested by query (flow sharing context, bulk SOQL behavior, email limits, default sender). Four such claims accrued across R halves, which triggered the optional T skip; it is unclear whether uncheckable-but-documented platform corrections should count toward the four-claim threshold the same way as query-contradicted facts.
Timing the D1 timeout: the MCP call timed out at ~74s; the skill's retry guidance says 'narrower', but D1 has a fixed 300-word template; guidance on which D1 return items to drop first would help.

Asking about both recipient and data shape used two of the three questions; scope.md says structure is decided, but 'runs low' threshold semantics (per-item vs global) is a business value, so the boundary between the two was a judgment call.
